source.anchor_kjv: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
source.thread: Jonah went down guilty for his own sin; Christ went down innocent bearing ours - and rose the third day. Jesus names Jonah as THE sign (Matt 12:40)
source.hook_line: I told the sailors to throw me into the sea — and a great fish swallowed me whole, and buried me alive in the dark.
source.spoken_script: I told the sailors to throw me into the sea — and a great fish swallowed me whole, and buried me alive in the dark. I ran from God because His mercy was too wide. He sent me to Nineveh, the city I hated — I'd sooner drown than see her spared. The storm came for my sake; the lot fell on me. To spare the sailors, I had them throw me overboard. Three days buried alive in the fish. Then, long after I was dust, scribes demanded a sign — Jesus gave them only my name: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth. I went down guilty — the storm was mine. He went down innocent, bearing what was ours; He gave Himself. The grave no more held Him than the deep held me. He rose. You who are sure you've fallen too far — that is how far His mercy reaches. It cost Him the grave. Stop running, and turn: the One who went down into your dark and rose again is Jesus. Come up out of the deep, and live.

platforms.title: Asked for a Miracle, Jesus Gave Them a Drowned Prophet
platforms.description:
The sign of Jonah (Matthew 12:40), told by the man who lived it.

I told the sailors to throw me into the sea, and a great fish swallowed me whole and buried me alive in the dark. I ran from God because his mercy was too wide: he sent me to Nineveh, the city I hated. The storm came for my sake. Three days buried alive in the fish.

Long after I was dust, scribes demanded a sign, and Jesus gave them only my name: "For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth" (Matthew 12:40, KJV).

I went down guilty; the storm was mine. He went down innocent, bearing what was ours. And the grave no more held him than the deep held me. He rose.

You who are sure you have fallen too far: that is how far his mercy reaches. It cost him the grave. Stop running, and turn. Come up out of the deep, and live.

platforms.title: The Sign of Jonah: The Only Miracle Jesus Promised the Scribes
platforms.description:
When the scribes and Pharisees demanded a sign (Matthew 12:40), Jesus refused every spectacle and gave them one name: Jonah.

"For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth" (Matthew 12:40, KJV).

This piece tells the sign from inside it, in Jonah's own voice. The prophet who ran, not from hardship, but from mercy: God sent him to Nineveh, the city he hated, and he would sooner drown than watch her spared. The storm that came for his sake. The lot that fell on him. The sailors he told to throw him overboard. And the great fish: three days buried alive in the dark.

Then the turn Jesus builds on: Jonah went down guilty, for his own storm. Christ went down innocent, bearing what was ours. Jonah was spat out alive; Christ walked out of the tomb. The grave no more held him than the deep held Jonah.

In this piece: Jonah's flight and confession in his own words, why Jesus chose this of all signs, and the mercy so wide a prophet ran from it - the same mercy that reaches whoever is sure they have fallen too far.

It cost him the grave. Stop running, and turn. Come up out of the deep, and live.

VERDICT: PASS

- Verbatim: the Matthew 12:40 anchor ("For as Jonas was three days and three nights in
  the whale's belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the
  heart of the earth") is character-exact KJV everywhere quoted, including the KJV
  spelling "Jonas". Clean.
- Ref front-load: "(Matthew 12:40)" sits in the first sentence of youtube_short,
  youtube_long, facebook and instagram. Clean.
- Typography: all-ASCII. Clean.
- Voice: the first-person witness copy mirrors the video's eyewitness format and is
  clearly framed ("told by the man who lived it" / "in Jonah's own voice") so the
  reader is never misled about who speaks. Good.
- Doctrine: "went down guilty vs went down innocent" is the piece's own thread;
  "the grave no more held him than the deep held me" is faithful; mercy-wide CTA is
  grace-anchored with no fear framing. "Asked for a Miracle, Jesus Gave Them a Drowned
  Prophet" is blunt but true to Matt 12:39-40's refusal of a sign except Jonah -
  honest curiosity, not clickbait. Jonah did not literally drown; the video's own
  imagery is buried-alive-in-the-deep, and "drowned prophet" is within its poetic
  register - acceptable, but if the gate's doctrine pass objects, swap to "a buried
  prophet". Not blocking.
